subject: Forensic liaison scheduling and DPA exception request — FinLane evidence transfer
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rios <emily.rios@finlane.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Forensic liaison scheduling and DPA exception request — FinLane evidence transfer

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To keep momentum, we need to lock down a few operational details so our team can prepare an evidence export without blocking on legal. Quick summary of what we need to confirm from your side:

- Do you require a formal DPA amendment (DocuSign) to allow cross-border transfer of a forensic snapshot, or will the existing DPA suffice with an exception ticket?
- Will FinLane accept a redacted snapshot (PII masked) initially, or do you require a full ingest-level export for triage?
- Preferred transfer mechanism: SFTP endpoint (EU) with AES-256 vs. encrypted signed transfer to an escrow provider. Any endpoint details you can share?
- Which FinLane point(s) will be the canonical forensic liaison and legal reviewer for this export?

Operational ask from Redwood: if you agree, we can nominate Marissa Cole as the forensic liaison on our side and Kimberly will be the privacy lead for any DPA amendments or scope exceptions. Proposed scheduling window: we can prepare a canary snapshot within 24–48 hours and a full evidence package within 48–96 hours depending on jurisdictional holds.

I attached a small manifest template (forensic_manifest_template.csv) that lists the data categories and typical export artifacts to speed technical acceptance. Please review and tell us what you need changed.

If you prefer, we can start the DocuSign amendment in parallel — just point us to the right legal contact.

Thanks,

— Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Rios <emily.rios@finlane.com>
To: Priya Naranjan <priya_naranjan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Forensic liaison scheduling and DPA exception request — FinLane evidence transfer

Priya —

Appreciate the summary and the manifest. High level answers below; I copied Security Ops (securityops@bluepeak.com) because they will own ingestion/handling on our side.

- DPA amendment: Legal will require a short amendment that calls out the transfer purpose and the escrow/SFTP recipient. We can accept a DocuSign amendment — please send the draft to legal@finlane.com.
- Redacted vs full export: For initial triage we will accept a redacted snapshot (remove direct identifiers) plus associated telemetry. If escalation is needed, we will request a controlled full export under a more restrictive access agreement.
- Transfer mechanism: We prefer an EU-based SFTP endpoint (AES-256) managed by our partner DataTransit. If needed we can accept a temporary escrow upload; security will share endpoint details.
- Liaison/legal contacts: Security contact is me (Lead Security Manager). Legal is Rachel Lim (rachel.lim@finlane.com). Security Ops (cc) will provide the SFTP details and the data acceptance checklist.

I attached our export requirements and a short checklist (finlane_data_export_requirements.pdf). We can sign the amendment once we have the transfer details and a nominated Redwood liaison.

Emily Rios
Lead Security Manager, FinLane

Emily —

Thanks for the clarity. A couple of notes from the privacy/legal side before we kick off ingestion:

- Redwood's standard DPA contains an Incident Notification and Data Transfer clause (Section 5.2 in our template). For cross-border forensic transfers we follow our internal exception process (internal ticket + legal sign-off). We will prepare a 1–2 page amendment that references the specific export artifacts and transfer endpoint.
- Masking: we can provide a redacted snapshot (hashes + pseudonymization of direct identifiers) as the default. Please confirm which specific attributes you consider "direct identifiers" so our manifest mapping is aligned.
- Timing: operationally, we can produce a canary snapshot within 24 hours of receiving endpoint credentials and a full package within 72–96 hours if no legal hold is required. If a judicial or supervisory hold applies, timelines will extend; please flag any jurisdictional constraints.
- Subprocessors: we will include a short subprocessors list with the export (DataTransit, CloudTransit Ltd., and ArchiveVault) and can add contractual attestations where needed.

We are nominating Marissa Cole as Redwood's forensic liaison (technical lead for packaging and transfer). Marissa, please confirm availability for a 30-minute handshake call (preferably today or first thing Monday). I attached our liaison roster for information (redwood_forensic_liaison_roster.pdf).

— Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Legal
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly and team — a couple of operational follow-ups:

- Security Ops will provide an EU SFTP endpoint (host and user) by EOD. Standard requirement: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, and HMAC verification for each package.
- Legal (Rachel) will expect the DPA amendment to reference: scope of data, retention period of the snapshot (we typically request 90 days), and an access roster for named individuals.
- Subprocessors: we need a formal list and brief description of roles for each subprocessor (hosting, transfer, long-term storage). The list will be attached to the amendment.
- Evidence format: CSV exports + compressed tar.gz of raw telemetry; an accompanying manifest (the template you sent is helpful).

I'll start the DocuSign workflow for an amendment (link below) once I have the SFTP details and your nominee for the access roster. Security Ops (cc) will reach out with the endpoint.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/FAKEID12345

Regards,

Emily Rios
Lead Security Manager, FinLane
